subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw doctor --fix 4-5x slower on 2026.5.20 vs 2026.5.19 (55s → 229s+) — session snapshot path traversal bottleneck

question: Should maintainers treat the current snapshot repair as enough to close this issue, or keep it open until the remaining doctor/update slowdown is proven fixed with live timing evidence?
rationale: The code now fixes the stale snapshot subset, but the issue's broader 4-5x slowdown is not proven resolved and the active candidate PR is blocked on proof plus ordering risk.

options.title: Keep Open For Measured Fix
options.body: Keep this issue canonical while maintainers repair or replace the open doctor optimization PR and require redacted before/after timing proof.

options.title: Close After Live Release Proof
options.body: Close only if maintainers can show current release or current main no longer reproduces the reported multi-session update slowdown.

options.title: Split Remaining Work
options.body: Close the stale snapshot portion as fixed and open a narrower follow-up for repair-sequencing or gateway reconnect performance.

recommendation.title: Keep Open For Measured Fix
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical while maintainers repair or replace the open doctor optimization PR and require redacted before/after timing proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the strongest ownership signal across doctor repair sequencing and session/auth migration surfaces.
